THE NEWSPAPERS' PLACE VOCABULARY, RESOLVED AGAINST THE COMMITTED TOWN (T-1048, of T-1047, of T-1040). Every DISTINCT `associated_places` string the newspapers gazetteer prints, resolved to `inside` the town, `outside` it, or `undecided` — and undecided is a real answer here, counted in `counts` and never folded into either neighbour.

WHY PER STRING AND NOT PER PERSON. The printed string is what is being read. Two records that print the same words are the same reading and must not be resolved apart, so the ruling attaches to the words; `resolve_place_vocabulary.person_resolution()` is what carries a string's answer up to a man, and it is deliberately generous — one place inside the town makes the man inside it, whatever else his record holds.

DERIVED FIRST, RULED ONLY WHERE DERIVATION CANNOT REACH. An entry carrying `derived` was resolved by `resolve_place_vocabulary.derive()` against the committed dataset alone — the bare town, `fronting_street.streets_named()`, a committed structure name or aka, or the town standing as the string's own comma qualifier — and is NOT hand-authored: `--check` re-derives every one of them and fails if the dataset has moved underneath it. An entry carrying `basis` is a RULING this project makes, under one of the boundaries below, with its reasoning in `note`. A derivation can only ever say `inside`: the committed dataset is the town, and it is silent about every place on earth it does not model, so 'Detroit' is not outside the town BECAUSE the dataset lacks it.

NOTHING HERE REFUSES ANYBODY. T-1048 settles the vocabulary and changes no card. T-1049 is the ticket that spends it, and the reason this file exists first is that the naive test refuses `Fort Dearborn`, `Water Street`, `the Mansion House` and `the corner of Water and Franklin streets, Chicago` — all of them inside the town it is modelling.

WHAT IT MOVES, and the whole of T-1048's argument. Of the 193 persons the naive test refuses, this resolution refuses 141. The other 52 are 27 it places INSIDE the town and 25 it will not decide — so a guard built on the naive test would have thrown about a fiftieth of the gazetteer's placed persons out of the town they lived in. All eight false positives T-1047's acceptance names resolve inside. `tools/resolve_place_vocabulary.py --report` restates every count in this file from the gazetteer and the committed town, and `counts` below is checked against it in the gate, so no number here can go stale without failing a commit.
generated_by: hand-authored rulings (T-1048); `tools/resolve_place_vocabulary.py --write` recomputes the `derived` entries and `counts`, and `--check` holds the whole file to the gazetteer and to the committed town in the gate
not_a_reading: an adjudication of readings this project already holds, not a fresh reading of a source. No entry here is evidence of anything; it says only what a place string this project has already read MEANS about the town.
counts_are: measured, not asserted: `--check` recomputes every field of `counts` from the gazetteer and the rulings and fails the gate on any disagreement

boundaries.B1: DERIVED — the committed dataset resolves the string on its own (D1 bare town, D2 a committed 1835 street via `streets_named()`, D3 a committed structure name or aka, D4 the bare town standing as one of the string's comma segments). Carried as `derived`, never hand-authored, re-derived by `--check`.
boundaries.B2: OUTSIDE — a place beyond the platted town and the military reservation that does NOT contain them: another settlement, county, state, territory or nation, or a named natural feature lying outside. A reading that names only such places is not a Chicago appearance.
boundaries.B3: INSIDE, RULED — a place within the town the derivation cannot spell: the fort or one of its parts under a short name; a town institution, landmark or business premises the corpus names in prose; a street or corner named without the word 'street', or named ambiguously between two committed streets that are BOTH in the town.
boundaries.B4: UNDECIDED — the string does not decide the question, and this project will not guess it. Three kinds land here: a container that HOLDS the town (a county, a state, a nation, an army), which places a man neither in the town nor out of it; a place the scene does not commit and cannot locate ('Main Street'); and a survey adjacent to the town that this project commits none of (Kinzie's Addition, Wabansia — T-0789, T-0790).
boundaries.B5: A LIVE IDENTITY QUESTION DOES NOT MAKE A PLACE UNDECIDED. Which house 'Eagle Tavern' names is T-0391's question; that it stood in the town is not in doubt, and the location is ruled while the identity stays open. `tickets` names the ticket that owns the rest.

This note used to read 'Undecided until the survey is drawn'; the survey is drawn — T-1070 seated Wabansia's seven streets and its block grid on the committed `kinzie` line, and T-1086 seated its river-front water lots and closed its tract outline, 78.63 acres of it, off the same datum. So the ground this vocabulary said it could not resolve against is committed, and the ruling is left standing anyway: `inside` or `outside` is a B-rule, the B-rules are the owner's, and moving a place off B4 changes what counts as a Chicago appearance. What the change would cost is now MEASURED rather than feared — ONE person in the whole register names Wabansia, `person_uncertain_doctor_kimberly` from the Democrat of 16 July 1834, and Wabansia is the only place the register has for him, so he is the entire re-scoring. T-1087 carries the question to the owner with the counts.

This file answers the second question and leaves the first refused.

T-1047's acceptance names this string among those a guard must not refuse, and that is the reading taken here.
